annotation.title_clean: Artificial intelligence act and regulatory sandboxes
annotation.title_en: Artificial intelligence act and regulatory sandboxes
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliamentary Research Service (Madiega, T.; Van De Pol, A.L.)
annotation.venue: European Parliament Think Tank (EPRS Briefing PE 733.544)
annotation.summary_en: European Parliamentary Research Service briefing on AI regulatory sandboxes in the Commission's 2021 AI Act proposal. It explains sandbox benefits and risks, Articles 53-55 provisions, and policy debates on liability, harmonisation and data protection. Embodied AI is only mentioned in passing (autonomous cars, drones as sandbox testbeds).
key_provisions_or_claims: Draft AI Act Articles 53-54 encourage Member States to set up coordinated AI regulatory sandboxes.
Sandbox participants remain liable for harm under applicable EU and national law (Art. 53(4)).
Data protection authorities must be associated with sandbox operation; further processing of personal data is allowed for public-interest AI development.
SMEs and start-ups get priority access to sandboxes (Art. 55).
Concerns include regulatory arbitrage, lack of liability protection, and single-market fragmentation.
